glosses: to conflict (with), to clash (with), to come up (against)
разг. быть в состоянии конфликта или вступать в конфликт с кем-либо, чем-либо

examples.text: Много дней подряд я конфликтую с этим актером.
Но зачем ссориться и конфликтовать из-за пустяков?

glosses: A clash or disagreement, often violent, between two or more opposing groups or individuals.

examples.text: The conflict between the government and the rebels began three years ago.

One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools[…]as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to school. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.

glosses: An incompatibility, as of two things that cannot be simultaneously fulfilled.

examples.text: I wanted to attend the meeting but there's a conflict in my schedule that day.

glosses: To be at odds (with); to disagree or be incompatible

examples.text: [T. E.] Lawrence said that in the end he felt himself to be fighting not for the imperial British but for the rebellious Arabs. All too often he conflicted with British bureaucratic fustiness.

glosses: To overlap (with), as in a schedule.

examples.text: Your conference call conflicts with my older one: please reschedule.
It appears that our schedules conflict.

glosses: A loud sound, like the crashing together of metal objects; a crash.

examples.text: I heard a clash from the kitchen, and rushed in to find the cat had knocked over some pots and pans.
Alone amid clashes of rain against the house.

glosses: A skirmish, a hostile encounter.

examples.text:
In Anatolia tensions between state officials (ehl-i örf) and the peasants were strained to breaking point.
At several places—particularly in the frontier provinces—there were fierce clashes between the janissaries stationed there and the governors. In Aleppo and Damascus incidents were common after 1589: the kuls threw rocks at the beylerbeyi’s house, killed people, broke into the divan several times and took the money prepared by the council for remittance to the centre.

glosses: match; a game between two sides.

examples.text: But they ran out of time and inspiration as Les Bleus set up a deserved semi-final clash with Wales.

glosses: An angry argument.
Opposition; contradiction; such as between differing or contending interests, views, purposes etc.

examples.text: clash of beliefs
culture clash

glosses: A combination of garments that do not look good together, especially because of conflicting colours.

examples.text: She was wearing a horrible clash of red and orange.

glosses: An instance of restarting the game after a \"dead ball\", where it is dropped between two opposing players, who can fight for possession.
Chatter; gossip; idle talk.
A heavy fall (of rain); heavy rain.

examples.text: clay soils ploughed in Autumn must often meet with heavy clashes of rain before frost: therefore , those salutary effects, expected to be derived from a frosty Winter, must often be frustrated, by the land being too much condensed by the rains before the frost comes on.
T' taties offer't ta be a grand crop et forend, bet then seea mitch clash an caald wes again em, an thaev tean up varra smo, […]

glosses: To make a clashing sound.

examples.text: The cymbals clashed.

glosses: To cause to make a clashing sound.

examples.text: Thorfinn clashed his shield against Vallon's and swung his axe to hook Vallon's ankle.

glosses: To come into violent conflict.

examples.text: Fans from opposing teams clashed on the streets after the game.

glosses: To argue angrily.

examples.text: My parents often clashed about minor things, such as the cleaning or shopping rota.

glosses: To face each other in an important game.

examples.text: The veteran American legend claims he and Welsh two-weight world champion Calzaghe will clash on 20 September, probably at The MGM Grand in Las Vegas.

glosses: To fail to look good together; to contrast unattractively; to fail to harmonize.

examples.text: You can't wear that shirt! It clashes with your trousers.
The hotel room was ugly, and the wallpaper clashed with the carpet.

glosses: To coincide, to happen at the same time, thereby rendering it impossible to attend all.

examples.text: I can't come to your wedding because it clashes with a friend's funeral.
I wanted to take German, but it clashed with art on the timetable.

glosses: To chatter or gossip.
To play Clash Royale or Clash of Clans.

examples.text: Dude, are we clashing tonight?
Let's clash before bedtime.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see come, up.

examples.text: I came up the ladder carefully, holding the bucket in my right hand.

glosses: To come towards; to approach.

examples.text: I was standing on the corner when Nick came up and asked for a cigarette.
Racing around to come up behind you again

glosses: To emerge or become known, especially unexpectedly.

examples.text: Unless anything comes up, I'll be there every day this week.

glosses: To be revealed to have a certain value, quality, or status.

examples.text: The movie didn't come up to our expectations.
Hey look Ma, I made it / Hey look Ma, I made it / Everything's comin' up aces, aces / If it's a dream, don't wake me, don't wake me

glosses: To come to attention and present oneself; to arrive or appear.

examples.text: At some point in the conversation my name came up, and I readily agreed to their proposition.
Be ready for when your turn comes up.
The proposal came up before the committee.
It is interesting that this argument should have come up at this moment," Mr. Smith adds, "when the subject is being debated so hotly in the field of the petrol-driven internal combustion engine."

glosses: To appear (before a judge or court).

examples.text: He came up before a judge and was fined a thousand dollars.

glosses: To draw near in time.

examples.text: The summer holidays are coming up.

glosses: To approach a time or scheduled event.

examples.text: We're coming up on the interview in the last half-hour of the program.

glosses: To reach in height.

examples.text: You have to come up to here to ride this roller-coaster.
He only comes up around this high.

glosses: To rise (above the horizon).

examples.text: It'll be warmer once the sun comes up.

glosses: To begin to feel the effects of a recreational drug.

examples.text: I could tell from her expression that she was coming up already.

glosses: To arrive at the university. (Compare go down, send down.)
To happen or occur.

examples.text: His shift came up, so he had to go to work.

glosses: To grow up; to experience a childhood.

examples.text: I came up in Baltimore.

glosses: To do well or be successful.

examples.text: Watch out for him, he's been coming up lately.

glosses: An opportunity

examples.text:
I'm gonna pop some tags
Only got 20$ in my pocket
I'm, I'm, I'm huntin', lookin' for a come up
This is fucking awesome

glosses: (di veicoli) andare addosso a qualcosa con veemenza
essere in conflitto o in incompatibilità, scontrarsi, combattersi

examples.text: il tuo e il mio sono due concetti che sono destinati a confliggere

glosses: strijden, botsen, niet samen kunnen gaan

examples.text: Finlands hoogste punt ligt op een helling, vlak onder een bergtop. Die top (Halti, 1.331 meter hoog) ligt in Noorwegen, 30 meter verderop. Een raar foutje van de achttiende-eeuwse kaartenmakers, vindt Bjørn Geirr Harsson, gepensioneerd geofysicus van de Noorse Landmeetkundige Dienst. Hoe leuk zou het zijn, om die bergtop aan Finland cadeau te geven, zodat Finlands hoogste punt een piek is? Noorwegen heeft bergen genoeg, en Finland viert dit jaar zijn 100-jarige onafhankelijkheid van Rusland. De grens een pietsie opschuiven - dat was alles. Ruim 17.000 mensen steunden zijn idee via een Facebookpagina; de burgemeester van de Noord-Noorse gemeente stuurde een voorstel naar Oslo. Eind 2016 kwam het teleurstellende antwoord. Nei da, Noorwegen gaat de grens niet verleggen. Dat zou conflicteren met Artikel 1 van de Grondwet, dat stelt dat Noorwegen ‘ondeelbaar en onoverdraagbaar’ is.

In het document staat wat de autolobbyist op 11 januari te horen kreeg van de ambtenaar, namelijk tot welke compromissen de Commissie bereid is. Die standpunten conflicteren met de officiële standpunten die de Commissie toen uitdroeg. Het gaat onder meer over toegestane foutmarge van de tests en de positie van lidstaat Spanje.
